title: The Dimension-Degree Boundary for Gaussian Moment Vanishing
summary: Determines the complex Gaussian dimension-degree boundary and proves the sharp ternary-cubic mixed-moment cutoff.
verification: Internally audited standalone manuscript with recorded proof, source and layout checks; publication and independent external review are still pending.
next_steps: Specialist review of the explicit degree-one nearby-cycle/chain comparison, finite-target infinity exclusion and regular-rank ledger, and relative-pair identification in the uniform-cut argument.
Independent review of the complete qualitative cubic classification and its cited analytic inputs before submission.
abstract:
We classify complex polynomials of degree at most three in three
independent standard real Gaussian variables whose positive moments all
vanish. Up to a complex orthogonal linear change of coordinates and a
nonzero scalar, every such polynomial has one-sided circular support or
belongs to a single exceptional orbit. For every fixed polynomial $Q$,
its mixed moments $\E[QP^m]$ vanish whenever $m>3\deg Q$, and the
coefficient three is optimal. The proof extracts a Gaussian coordinate
in which the polynomial is affine linear, then classifies that family
using formal stationary frames and analytic period estimates.

Combining this ternary-cubic result with Wilson's two-variable theorem,
Liu's quadratic theorem and Long's counterexamples gives the exact
dimension--degree boundary for the Gaussian Moments Conjecture: the
implication from pure-moment vanishing to eventual mixed-moment
vanishing holds universally precisely when there are at most two
variables, the degree is at most two, or there are three variables and
the degree is at most three. We reproduce the all-order moment
identities for the two minimal failures.
